title: What the live paper record shows
description: The engines' own state, read from the running record: what is open, what closed, and what the market filter is doing right now.
body:
Paper signals only. No real orders are placed anywhere in this record. The engines' own state is read from the running record: what is open, what closed, and what the market filter is doing right now. v005 counts its live record from 1 October 2026 and v006 from 9 October 2026. This live snapshot was read at 2026-11-17T09:17:30.804Z.

## Framing and scope

Every position in this record is paper, and one trade says nothing about a strategy. The paper-only boundary is the condition under which every number in the record was produced: no real orders are placed anywhere in this record, so the entries, exits, and percentages describe simulated positions only. The record is early. v005 began on 1 October 2026 and v006 on 9 October 2026. The initial live signal was an ATOM entry at 2.066 after the 10 October 2026 daily close. ATOM exited below its 10-day low at the 18 October 2026 close, at 1.703, which is −17.9% after the 30 bps round trip. A NEAR entry at 5.896 on 12 October 2026 has been open since. In testing, a losing start was the expected case rather than a surprise, and the average winner was roughly +19%.

The framing matters because the live window is short and the sample is small. A single closed trade, whether it gains or loses, cannot establish how either engine behaves across market conditions. The record should be read as a running log of paper signals, not as evidence of an edge.

## Open positions and recent closes

htf-rsi-v007 reports 0 positions open on paper and 4 closed trades so far, with an average null net per trade. trend-daily-v005 reports 0 positions open on paper and 6 closed trades so far, with an average −13.22% net per trade. trend-daily-v006 reports 0 positions open on paper and 7 closed trades so far, with an average −13.34% net per trade. The open position described in the record is the NEAR entry at 5.896 from 12 October 2026.

htf-rsi-v007, trend-daily-v005, and trend-daily-v006 are separate engines with separate counts. Their closed-trade totals are 4, 6, and 7, and their open-position counts are all 0. The averages differ: null for htf-rsi-v007, −13.22% for v005, and −13.34% for v006. Those differences are part of the record, but with so few trades they do not support a ranking.

The closed-trade averages are negative measurements of completed paper trades after costs. They describe what happened in this small live window; they do not estimate future results. The NEAR position remains open, so it has no closed-trade result yet and is not included in those averages.

## Market filter and breakout distances

Both trend engines report the Bitcoin market filter is off. trend-daily-v005 has 0 positions open on paper, and trend-daily-v006 has 0 positions open on paper. With the filter off, the record shows no open trend positions and no new breakout entries being recorded.

The filter being off is a state, not an explanation by itself. The record shows the state and the resulting absence of open trend positions, but it does not show why the filter is off or when it will change. Any statement about future filter behavior would be a prediction, and this article makes none.

The engines also report how far selected symbols are from their 20-day breakout:

- trend-daily-v005: TRXUSDT is 13.39% below its high; ATOMUSDT is 18.95% below its high; AAVEUSDT is 19.40% below its high.
- trend-daily-v006: TRXUSDT is 13.39% below its high; JUPUSDT is 14.56% below its high; ATOMUSDT is 18.95% below its high.

These distances are measurements from the current price to the reported high. They show how far each symbol remains from the breakout level while the filter is off. They are not signals to buy or sell, and they do not predict whether the level will be reached.

## Record continuity

The record updates continuously. The same numbers appear on the performance page, in the signal log, and in the status posted to the channel. Because every entry and exit is paper, the log can be checked against those sources without any real order having been placed. Readers can follow the same sequence from the initial ATOM entry at 2.066 through the ATOM exit at 1.703 and the open NEAR entry at 5.896, then compare those events with the closed-trade averages and the breakout distances. The value of the record is that the same figures appear in multiple places, which makes the paper trail checkable. This live snapshot was read at 2026-11-17T09:17:30.804Z.
